Team — quick summary from the bridge (runtime + infra):

What we observed:
- At 07:36 PT the Dedicated GPU pool serving PP-492 started showing persistent queue depths on worker VMs. Queueing correlated with sharp increase in per-token latencies and 5xx responses.
- Telemetry: observed an abrupt rise in KV-cache eviction pressure on the node set (kv_evictions/sec + cache_miss_rate increased ~6x). The worker serving path shows a long tail in model recv/send latency.
- Reservation check: PP-492's reserved throughput was within configured limits, but effective available capacity dropped due to multi-tenant resource contention (a co-resident tenant triggered heavy bursty key-value cache usage and continuous batching patterns that monopolized GPU memory and scheduling).
- Autoscaler actions: autoscaler attempted to add headroom but was rate-limited by our allocation policies for the Dedicated pool — new nodes did not come online fast enough to prevent queueing.

Immediate recommended mitigations (short-term, 0–3 hours):
A) Authorize an emergency burst add (heightened capacity) to the region for PP-492 while we rebalance. This requires Ops/Finance approval.
B) Apply a targeted per-tenant token-rate throttle for the noisy neighbor (identified tenant id T-881) and re-route its best-effort traffic to a lower-priority pool to free headroom for reserved tenants.
C) Roll back the recent model rollout (redwood/open-llama-13b-v1-s2) that increased per-request memory pressure for a subset of customers — scheduling rollback for the next 15 minutes unless infra says otherwise.
D) Enable temporary aggressive KV cache pinning for PP-492 (reduce eviction rate) to restore hit-rate.
E) Offer PrimePay a service credit for the window if we cannot restore within 90 minutes; Sales to approve.

Attachments pulled to the incident channel (for context): reservation_usage_snapshot.csv, kv_cache_trace.txt, primepay_peak_requests.png
